story: Tangaroa, the great god of the sea, is the son of Sky and Earth. Together with his brothers, the gods of forests, cultivated foods, wild foods, and war, he helped forcibly separate their parents. Afterward, the god of storms attacked him in fury, forcing Tangaroa to flee and hide within the sea. Tangaroa became the father of many sea creatures. His son had two children: one became the ancestor of all fish, the other the ancestor of all reptiles. Terrified by the storm god's onslaught, the fish took refuge in the sea while the reptiles fled to the forests. Because the forest god sheltered these runaway reptiles, Tangaroa has held a lasting grudge against him. This rivalry reflects a belief that the sea and the land are opposed realms, so people who go fishing or travel by sea are seen as entering the domain of the sea god, the enemy of the forest god who claims humans as his own; for this reason, offerings must be made to Tangaroa before any sea voyage. In another tradition, a trickster hero seeks fire from Tangaroa, who is said to be the origin of fire. Advised to reach Tangaroa's home by the safe path, the hero instead takes the forbidden path of death, enraging Tangaroa, who tries to kick him to death. The hero fights back, forces Tangaroa to give him fire, and kills him. When the parents of the hero are horrified, he uses magical chants to bring Tangaroa back to life.
